 Instron® | 9400 Series Drop Weight Impact Testing Machines
 Instron® | 9400 Series Drop Weight Impact Testing Machines
The 9400 Series Drop Weight Impact Testing Machines comes in a range of capacities up to 24 m/s impact speed and provide exceptional performance with unparalleled accuracy and reliability. It is capable of performing various impact tests methods, including puncture, compression after impact, tensile, 3 point bending, adhesive peel, cushioning and component tests. The 9400 Series offers ultimate flexibility for any testing need.
Contact Us 
 Related Videos 
 Compression After Impact with a Drop Weight Impact Testing Machine
A CAI test (compression after impact test) is a two-step procedure that assesses the potential damage to composite materials. The CAI test procedure is described in the dedicated standards ASTM D7136M, ASTM D7136, ISO 18352 and Airbus AITM 1.0010. The first step involves using a drop weight impact machine to induce Barely Visible Impact Damage (BVID). This is followed by a compression test of the damaged coupon using an electromechanical machine.

 Bluehill Impact Tup Calibration Alert for Drop Weight Impact Tester
Automatic alerts are generated when Tup calibration period is expiring. This feature helps to reduce the risk of invalid tests and protect your results against inaccuracies.
 Watch
 DCPD Measurement for Fracture Toughness and Crack Growth
Measurements based on mechanical compliance are very well established and reliable, but some work requires more complex measurement solutions. This webinar provides an introduction to the practicalities of the DCPD measurement technique and how the raw data needs to be handled and analyzed in materials testing.

ASTM Standards
This section provides a curated overview of the most prominent and widely adopted ASTM standards relevant to the materials testing industry, offering professionals a reliable reference to support consistent practices, accurate results, and regulatory compliance across a wide range of applications. The standards included are selected based on their frequency of use, industry recognition, and relevance to core testing methods, ensuring that users are equipped with foundational guidelines for quality assurance and technical integrity.  Compression After Impact with a Drop Weight Impact Testing Machine
 Compression After Impact with a Drop Weight Impact Testing Machine
A CAI test (compression after impact test) is a two-step procedure that assesses the potential damage to composite materials. The CAI test procedure is described in the dedicated standards ASTM D7136M, ASTM D7136, ISO 18352 and Airbus AITM 1.0010. The first step involves using a drop weight impact machine to induce Barely Visible Impact Damage (BVID). This is followed by a compression test of the damaged coupon using an electromechanical machine.

 Impact Testing Systems
 Products

 Testing Systems
»
 Impact Testing Systems
Impact resistance is one of the most important properties for component designers to consider, and one of the most difficult to quantify. It's a critical measure of service life and carries significant implications for product safety and liability. Instron has more than 80 years of experience designing impact testing systems that simulate real-life impact conditions.
 Drop Weight Impact Testers
Instron Drop Towers are used to develop, fine-tune, and validate material models under high-rate impact conditions. The new 9400 Series produces reliable, repeatable results, whether you're testing materials and components before production to improve product acceptance or testing during production to ensure continuous improvement.
Drop weight testing is commonly used across automotive, packaging, consumer electronics, and materials research applications to evaluate how a product or material responds to a single, high-energy impact event — from a dropped phone to a vehicle component in a collision. Configurable drop height and impact mass let you tailor tests to a wide range of energy levels and specimen types, supporting standards such as ASTM D3763 and ISO 6603.
More Info 
 Pendulum Testers
Instron Pendulum Impact Testing Systems determine the impact resilience of plastics and composites safely and efficiently, complying with all major ISO and ASTM impact testing methods across an energy range of 0.5 to 50 J. It supports Charpy, Izod, and tensile impact testing in both manual and motorized configurations, making it well suited to quality control and material characterization work where repeatable, standards-compliant results are essential.
Unlike drop weight testing, which simulates a single high-energy impact event, pendulum impact testing measures the energy absorbed by a specimen during fracture — a key indicator of a material's toughness and resistance to sudden loading.
More Info 
 Out of Production Impact Drop Towers & Pendulums
All impact Instron Impact Testing systems produced from 1975. These include drop towers and pendulums, such as the Fractovis and Dynatup Series.
